issue_context.title: Package manager discovery makes incorrect assumptions about dnf availability
issue_context.body:
### Summary

fedora-minimal:38 minimal containers only contain microdnf which now points to dnf5. See https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Changes/MajorUpgradeOfMicrodnf. The package manager discovery code added https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/80272/ only selects dnf5 on Fedora >= 39 and doesn't consider it otherwise. In the fedora-minimal:38 container, `ansible_pkg_manager` is set to `unknown` when it should be set to `dnf5`.

Package manager discovery should **prefer** dnf5 on Fedora 39, but it shouldn't ignore dnf4 on Fedora >= 39 if dnf5 is missing (users can exclude dnf5 from their systems if they'd like), and it shouldn't ignore dnf5 on Fedora < 39 when dnf4 is missing (the fedora-minimal:38 container is one example of where this assumption breaks).

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

dnf5
lib/ansible/module_utils/facts/system/pkg_mgr.py

### Ansible Version

```console
$ ansible --version
ansible [core 2.15.0.dev0]
  config file = None
  configured module search path = ['/root/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /root/venv/lib64/python3.11/site-packages/ansible
  ansible collection location = /root/.ansible/collections:/usr/share/ansible/collections
  executable l\ocation = ./venv/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.11.2 (main, Feb  8 2023, 00:00:00) [GCC 13.0.1 20230208 (Red Hat 13.0.1-0)] (/root/venv/bin/python3)
  jinja version = 3.1.2
  libyaml = True
```


### Configuration

```console
# if using a version older than ansible-core 2.12 you should omit the '-t all'
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed -t all
CONFIG_FILE() = None
```


### OS / Environment

Fedora 38 instance with dnf5 but not dnf

### Steps to Reproduce

<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->
```Dockerfile
# fedora-minimal only has microdnf, which has been replaced by dnf5
FROM registry.fedoraproject.org/fedora-minimal:38

WORKDIR /root

RUN dnf5 install -qy python3 python3-libdnf5

RUN python3 -m venv venv && \
    ./venv/bin/pip install 'https://github.com/ansible/ansible/archive/devel.tar.gz'

RUN ./venv/bin/ansible --version

RUN ./venv/bin/ansible-config dump --only-changed -t all

RUN ./venv/bin/ansible -i localhost -c local localhost -m setup | grep pkg

RUN ./venv/bin/ansible -i localhost -c local localhost -m package -a name=zsh
```


### Expected Results

I expect ansible to determine that `ansible_pkg_manager` is dnf5 and use it as the backend for the `package` module.

The current logic is the standard logic we do for distributions, we just pick the default. For other cases we added the `use_backend` option to the `dnf` module for users to choose the appropriate backend.

We would have to add a specific logic for specific containers which would make the whole logic too complex and not easily maintainable.

Here is the current incorrect behavior:

| Fedora Version | dnf available (y/n) | dnf5 available (y/n) | `ansible_pkg_mgr` (current) | `ansible_pkg_mgr` (expected) |
| -------------- | ------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| <39            | y                   | n                    | dnf                         | dnf                          |
| <39            | y                   | y                    | dnf                         | dnf                          |
| <39            | n                   | y                    | **unknown**                     | dnf5                         |
| >=39           | n                   | y                    | **unknown**                     | dnf5                         |
| >=39           | y                   | y                    | dnf5                        | dnf5                         |
| >=39           | y                   | n                    | **dnf5**                        | dnf                          |


Something like this should do what's expected:

``` diff
diff --git a/lib/ansible/module_utils/facts/system/pkg_mgr.py b/lib/ansible/module_utils/facts/system/pkg_mgr.py
index bca283a8aa..f51075eaad 100644
--- a/lib/ansible/module_utils/facts/system/pkg_mgr.py
+++ b/lib/ansible/module_utils/facts/system/pkg_mgr.py
@@ -18,6 +18,7 @@ from ansible.module_utils.facts.collector import BaseFactCollector
 PKG_MGRS = [{'path': '/usr/bin/rpm-ostree', 'name': 'atomic_container'},
             {'path': '/usr/bin/yum', 'name': 'yum'},
             {'path': '/usr/bin/dnf', 'name': 'dnf'},
+            {'path': '/usr/bin/dnf5', 'name': 'dnf5'},
             {'path': '/usr/bin/apt-get', 'name': 'apt'},
             {'path': '/usr/bin/zypper', 'name': 'zypper'},
             {'path': '/usr/sbin/urpmi', 'name': 'urpmi'},
@@ -77,11 +78,10 @@ class PkgMgrFactCollector(BaseFactCollector):
                 if int(collected_facts['ansible_distribution_major_version']) < 23:
                     if self._pkg_mgr_exists('yum'):
                         pkg_mgr_name = 'yum'
-                elif int(collected_facts['ansible_distribution_major_version']) >= 39:
-                    # /usr/bin/dnf is planned to be a symlink to /usr/bin/dnf5
-                    if self._pkg_mgr_exists('dnf'):
-                        pkg_mgr_name = 'dnf5'
-                else:
+                elif int(collected_facts['ansible_distribution_major_version']) < 39:
+                    # Always use dnf if it's available.
+                    # dnf5 or yum may be installed on Fedora < 39,
+                    # but the system default should be prefered.
                     if self._pkg_mgr_exists('dnf'):
                         pkg_mgr_name = 'dnf'
             except ValueError:
```

review_comments: I'm not sure removing this is a good idea. /usr/bin/dnf5 will always be present if dnf5 is installed, but I don't think /usr/bin/dnf-3 is synonymous with dnf4. IMO, it would be better to keep this for distributions other than Fedora which we don't special case.

The intent behind removing `/usr/bin/dnf` from `PKG_MGRS` is trying to avoid potential false positives since there is no guarantee what `/usr/bin/dnf` is at this point.

> I don't think /usr/bin/dnf-3 is synonymous with dnf4

Can you be a more specific? Are you saying that `/usr/bin/dnf-3` doesn't have to necessarily exist for `dnf != 5`?

> distributions other than Fedora which we don't special case

We don't just "special case" Fedora, we do all of this dnf heuristic for "derivatives of RHEL". OpenMandriva which doesn't belong to that group and uses dnf seems to have `/usr/bin/dnf-3` present on the filesystem. Are there others?

> Can you be a more specific? Are you saying that `/usr/bin/dnf-3` doesn't have to necessarily exist for `dnf != 5`?

Exactly, /usr/bin/dnf-3 might not always exist when /usr/bin/dnf is version 4. AFAIK /usr/bin/dnf-2 and /usr/bin/dnf-3 were only created during the python2 -> python3 transition.

On the other hand, /usr/bin/dnf5 should always exist when dnf version 5 is installed.

Is `/usr/bin/dnf-2` actually used as a default package manager somewhere? We could add that to `PKG_MGR` just to be on the safe side. For `ansible_os_family == RedHat` the current code in the PR would still match `dnf` (dnf4) module for `/usr/bin/dnf-2` correctly.

I'm not sure about the exact history (might be a good idea to ask jmracek or someone else on that team), but according to the Fedora 22 dnf specfile [1], /usr/bin/dnf-2 was the default in Fedora 22 and /usr/bin/dnf-3 was the default in Fedora 23 and thereafter. In earlier releases, yum, not dnf, was the default package manager. However, RedHat-ish distributions are already special cased, and I have no idea about other distributions, so take that point for what you will.

In any case, this shouldn't be a problem for recent versions, so I'd rather merge this as is than have a long, drawn out discussion :smiley:.


[1] https://src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/dnf/blob/f22/f/dnf.spec#_170
This assumption won't work. On Fedora 38, if both microdnf and dnf4 are installed, dnf5 will be used, which is incorrect. dnf4 is the default on Fedora 38.

/usr/bin/dnf -> /usr/bin/dnf5 means that dnf5 is the default, but /usr/bin/microdnf -> /usr/bin/dnf5 does not. I can't think of a reasonable approach other than https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/80546/files#diff-8b63763b5cd493d8881baa72868750be9858f44056485d5ae0002de56994c009R81-R86 that handles using dnf4 on Fedora < 39 even if dnf5 is installed but works in the Fedora Minimal container.
Okay, the current code makes more sense. It only checks /usr/bin/microdnf if /usr/bin/dnf is missing.
